New Zealand.ttl: Seeds & Plants into New Zealand: Permit Rules 2026
New Zealand.desc: Bringing plants or seeds into New Zealand (2026): High-risk - usually needs a permit. Live plants, seeds, soil and cuttings are tightly controlled.
New Zealand.lead: New Zealand's Ministry for Primary Industries treats plants and plant products as biosecurity risk goods: every traveller fills in the New Zealand Traveller Declaration, and all plant material must be declared or put in an amnesty bin before inspection. Failing to declare can bring an instant NZD 400 fine, and some plant products are prohibited outright.

Risk goods you do not want inspected can be thrown into the marked bins at arrival to avoid a search or a fine

In general, if no import health standard covers an item, it cannot be brought into the country
Soil and equipment used with plants or outdoors are also listed as risk goods to declare

Not read: the detailed list of banned plant products and the seed-specific import health standards are on other MPI pages that we did not read.
faq: Can I bring seeds into New Zealand?

Seeds are listed by MPI as plant products you must declare. Whether a given seed is allowed depends on an import health standard, and an item with no standard cannot come in, so declare them and let an officer decide.
Do I have to declare plants at the New Zealand border?
Yes. All plant material, including flowers, bulbs, leaves and wood, must be declared on the New Zealand Traveller Declaration or put in an amnesty bin.
What is the fine for not declaring plants in New Zealand?

MPI says an undeclared biosecurity risk item, even by accident, can bring an instant NZD 400 fine; smuggling a prohibited or risk item can mean up to NZD 100,000, up to 5 years in prison and deportation.
Can I bring soil to New Zealand?
Soil is named as a risk item to declare, and used gardening or outdoor equipment must be declared as well.

Chile.ttl: Can You Bring Seeds & Plants into Chile? Permit Rules (2026)
Chile.desc: Bringing plants or seeds into Chile (2026): High-risk - usually needs a permit. Live plants, seeds, soil and cuttings are tightly controlled.
Chile.lead: Chile's agriculture service SAG requires everyone aged 18 or over to complete a sworn declaration on entry that lists live plants and plant parts, all grains and seeds, and soil or soil-containing products. Declaring does not guarantee entry: an SAG inspector decides whether each item meets the rules, and false information can be fined.

faq: Can I bring seeds into Chile?
Seeds of every kind, whether for eating or sowing, must be declared on the SAG sworn declaration, and an SAG inspector then decides if they can enter.
Do I need to declare plants when entering Chile?
Yes. Live plants and plant parts such as leaves, stems, roots, cuttings and bulbs must be declared, as must flowers, wood and cones.
Can I fill in the Chile declaration before the flight?
Yes, the online form can be completed up to one day before arrival, and a new form is needed every time you enter Chile.
What if I travel with a child?
Anyone responsible for a minor under 18 must list the contents of the child's luggage on their own form.

Hong Kong.date: AFCD page dated 23 February 2026, read 18 October 2026
Hong Kong.ttl: Can You Bring Seeds & Plants into Hong Kong? Permit Rules (2026)
Hong Kong.desc: Bringing plants or seeds into Hong Kong (2026): High-risk - usually needs a permit. Live plants, seeds, soil and cuttings are tightly controlled.
Hong Kong.lead: Under Hong Kong's Plant (Importation and Pest Control) Ordinance, a plant needs a Plant Import Licence from AFCD plus a valid phytosanitary certificate from the country of origin. Seeds are the easier case: no licence is needed if a valid phytosanitary certificate accompanies them. Several everyday items need neither document, including cut flowers and fruit or vegetables for eating.

Cut flowers; fruit and vegetables for eating; grains, pulses, seeds and spices for human or animal consumption or industrial use; timber, rattan and bamboo; dried tobacco; plants grown elsewhere in China and imported from there
Soil, sand, clay, peat and plant pests

faq: Can I bring seeds into Hong Kong?
Seeds need no Plant Import Licence when they come with a valid phytosanitary certificate from the country of origin. Seeds for eating or industrial use are exempt from both.
Do I need a permit to bring a plant into Hong Kong?
Yes, a Plant Import Licence from AFCD and a valid phytosanitary certificate are required for plants in general.
Can I bring cut flowers or fruit to Hong Kong?
AFCD lists cut flowers and fruit and vegetables for consumption among the items that need no licence or certificate.
Can I import soil into Hong Kong?
Soil, including earth, sand, clay and peat, needs authorisation from the Director of Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation, except soil from other places in China.

Iceland.lead: Iceland's food and veterinary authority MAST allows plants in only with a phytosanitary certificate from the exporting country (Regulation 189/1990), but travellers may carry small amounts of cut flowers, bulbs and indoor plants without one. Wild plants, woody plants, bonsai and potatoes fall outside that allowance, and a list of tree species is banned entirely.

MAST does not list seeds among the banned plants, but its plant import page gives no traveller allowance for them either. It says only that Iceland applies EC seed legislation, so ask MAST before bringing more than a small personal amount.
Can I bring flowers to Iceland?
Yes, bouquets of cut flowers and branches up to 25 plants can travel with you without a phytosanitary certificate.
Can I bring a potted plant to Iceland?
A few potted indoor plants from Europe, up to 3 pieces, can come without a certificate; woody plants and bonsai are excluded from that allowance.
Which plants are banned in Iceland?
MAST lists elm, birch, pine, spruce, larch, willow and poplar, fir for planting, other conifers from outside Europe and wild-collected plants, among others.

The list covers plants, cuttings, bulbs, cut flowers and seeds, even commercially packaged ones.

Seeds, including commercially packaged ones, are on the MRA list of goods you declare and that the Ministry of Agro-Industry and Food Security must clear before Customs releases them.
Can I bring plants or cuttings to Mauritius?
Plants, cuttings, roots, bulbs and live ornamentals must be declared and cleared by the Ministry; the page does not say how to apply.
Is fruit allowed into Mauritius?
All fresh fruit and vegetables are on the declaration and clearance list, as are dried ones that contain seeds or skin.
Do orchids and cacti need a permit in Mauritius?
They can be restricted under CITES, which works with import and export permits.
